subject: humanities
passage: Amrita Sher-Gil, born in Budapest in 1913 to a Hungarian mother and a Sikh father, trained as a painter in Paris in the early 1930s and won early recognition there. Yet she felt that her real subject lay elsewhere. In 1934 she returned to India, and over the next seven years she painted villagers, musicians, and women at rest in flat planes of warm color that drew on both European modernism and the tradition of Indian miniature painting. By the time she died in Lahore in 1941, at only twenty-eight, she ______ a body of work that critics now place at the start of modern Indian art.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The phrase "By the time she died in Lahore in 1941" sets a point in the past, and the body of work was completed before that point. An action finished before another past action takes the past perfect: "had produced."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The simple past "produced" does not show that the work was already complete before she died; after "by the time," the earlier action needs the past perfect.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The present perfect "has produced" links an action to the present, but the sentence is anchored to a moment in 1941.
explanation.C: Correct. The past perfect "had produced" shows that the work was complete before the past moment "by the time she died."
explanation.D: Incorrect. The past progressive "was producing" describes an action still in progress, which contradicts the completed "body of work."

checks.note: had produced and produced both fit; past perfect is the tighter choice.
